# Scenario Clarification

## Frontend

- **Target framework**: Expo for iOS, Android, and web; complete visual redesign, best-in-class experience. The exact Expo SDK version is to be selected during implementation based on the repository and supported React Native/web dependencies.
- **Component library**: MUI, with a responsive design system suitable for the Expo web and administrative surfaces; use compatible React Native primitives where MUI web components do not apply.
- **Screenshots**: No external screenshots supplied; use the existing UI and requirements as the visual baseline.
- **Design system**: Match the existing experience where behavior or brand continuity requires it, while delivering the requested premium, fast, accessible BottleBazaar visual polish.
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA (default).
- **Browser targets**: Modern evergreen browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge, latest two major versions) (default).
- **Responsive strategy**: Mobile-first using existing breakpoints detected from the codebase (default), with deliberate iOS, Android, web, and admin adaptations.
- **i18n locales**: Preserve current locales and existing i18n library if present (default).
- **State management**: Preserve the existing pattern where identifiable; otherwise use minimal component state plus an appropriate server-state library (default).
- **Routing**: Use the de-facto router for the chosen Expo/React target and preserve compatible existing routes where applicable (default).

## Backend

- **Target framework**: Java with Spring Boot; select the compatible supported Spring Boot version during implementation.
- **API contract preservation**: Preserve existing contracts and extend compatibly. Existing client behavior and compatible code must continue to work.
- **Data migration strategy**: Create a fresh schema and seed data while preserving compatible code and existing behavior; use an additive, reversible migration/data transition approach where existing PostgreSQL data must be retained.
- **Auth framework**: Phone OTP plus email/password authentication, implemented with the repository-compatible Spring Security approach (default framework selection).
- **SLA targets**: Match the current production baseline with no regression (default).

## Generic

- **Success definition**: End-to-end modernization of BottleBazaar in place with behavioral correctness and visual polish. The launch-ready Sohna/Gurugram product must support customer discovery and in-store QR redemption; merchant stores, licenses, offers, inventory, and analytics; and admin moderation, dry-day/configuration controls, audit, and analytics. Authentication must support phone OTP and email/password. Payments and online redemption are out of scope.
- **Out of scope**: Payments and online redemption; redemption is in-store only. Do not blindly replace working code or unrelated functionality.
- **Existing test posture**: Run targeted builds and tests, with behavioral correctness as the acceptance bar and no regressions in preserved functionality.
- **Output location**: In place.
- **Additional constraints**: Do not blindly replace working code; preserve existing functionality and use the current stack unless necessary. Target launch is Sohna/Gurugram. Use Expo for iOS, Android, and web; migrate the backend to Java/Spring Boot; create a fresh schema and seed data while preserving compatible code. Deliver a premium, fast, accessible BottleBazaar design.
